column1: # Columns: issue_or_label<TAB>category. A number is a per-issue override; anything else is a label.
# An issue gets the category of its override, else of the first label row below that it carries
# (so the order of the label rows matters), else "Core". Category "-" leaves the issue out of the notes.
# Categories follow the topic groups of Godot's interactive changelog, in this order:
# 2D, 3D, Animation, Audio, Buildsystem, C#, Core, Editor, Export, GDExtension, GDScript, GUI, Import,
# Input, Navigation, Network, Physics, Platforms, Rendering, Shaders, Tests, Thirdparty, XR.
# Type: "type: feature" = Feature, "type: refactoring" = Enhancement, "type: bug" = Bugfix.
# "type: task" and "type: concept" appear (as Enhancement) only with an issue override here, since only
# the author knows whether they shipped code; without one they are left out. "type: review" and
